newsitem.title: USA: High-tech issues propel Nasdaq higher again.
newsitem.headline: High-tech issues propel Nasdaq higher again.

text.p: Continued strength in high technologies lifted the Nasdaq Composite to a higher close Wednesday, with Intel Corp leading the way.
The Nasdaq Composite was up 2.43 points, or 0.20 percent, at 1205.74 at its unofficial close. Declines led advances by 2114 to 1961 on volume of about 553 million shares.
Fueling the rally was an initial forecast by International Data Corp that it expected the U.S. personal computer industry to ship 13 percent more units next year than in 1996.
The announcement came a day after Intel said that its revenue would rise at least five percent sequentially in the third quarter. That sparked the rally in techs on Tuesday.

In addition to Intel, which rose 1-3/8 to 95-5/8 Wednesday and was the most actively traded issue on the Nasdaq, Microsoft Corp gained 2-5/8 at 136-1/2, Sun Microsystems rose 2-1/2 to 61 and Oracle Corp climbed 1-3/4 at 43-3/8.
Netscape Communications Corp fell 3-3/8 to 42-5/8 after Merrill Lynch downgraded the stock to near-term neutral from accumulate and to long-term neutral from buy.
